_comment: PRD section 2's performance budgets. Rule R-E: budgets are laws — a gate is
never edited to make a build pass. If a change cannot meet one, the change
is wrong or the budget needs an ADR; both are decisions, not edits.
IDLE RAM HAS TWO NAMES ON PURPOSE (ADR-017). They are different numbers and
conflating them is what produced a 300 MiB panic over a 116 MiB problem:
The PRD 1.5 metric. GPU-rendered, on the 10.2 low-end row. This is the
only number a release claim may cite.
The per-PR tripwire, measured on the llvmpipe VM we can actually run in
CI. COMPUTED from the two fields above, and deliberately never
written down anywhere as a number of its own — so the CI gate cannot
be moved without editing the offset's provenance record below and
saying what was re-measured. A test enforces its absence.
The offset is an empirical calibration constant, NOT a tunable. Per ADR-017
clause 3 it may only ever change to a newly measured pair — same build, both
renderers — taken at an M-gate, and drift over 25% is itself a finding to
investigate before the new value is adopted.

product.conditions: 2-minute settle after GUI login, 4 GB, GPU-rendered (ADR-017 clause 1)
product.canonical_seat: PRD 10.2 low-end row: 4 GB RAM, integrated GPU
product.interim_source: the owner's GPU-accelerated local VM (MERIDIAN_VM_GL=1, virgl), until that machine exists
product.note: 1.1 GiB = 1126 MiB. Measured as MemTotal - MemAvailable.

render_offset.method: paired measurement, same disk image, both renderers: llvmpipe mean 1424 MiB across 4 runs (1448.2 CI, 1414.0, 1436.6, 1397.5) minus virgl 1242.0 MiB
render_offset.recalibrate: at every M-gate (ADR-017 clause 3); >25% drift is a finding, not an update

boot_seconds.conditions: cold boot, power-on to login screen, virtio SSD VM (PRD 2)
boot_seconds.note: Read from systemd's own firmware+loader+kernel+userspace total. Host-page-cache sensitive: the same image measured 16.9 s cold and 7.8 s warm, so a single over-gate reading on a busy host is not by itself a regression.
